research_question: Can an answer-free event-role graph distinguish who owns a grounded action, what predicate a request marker governs, and whether the event is current, habitual, or past, thereby removing all three deterministic V58 external false actions without changing the model fallback, compiler, dataset, scorer, or any V58-correct result?
project_effect: This adds a bounded prerequisite for human-like language understanding: a request marker elsewhere in a sentence must not turn every mentioned action into a command. The system must bind an action to its actor, time, and governing speech act before authorizing a VRM action. It does not improve wording, memory, personality, reflection, VTuber imitation, or general intelligence.
expected_effect: Exactly three false-action targets should change from requested to mentioned. State correctness should rise from 82/87 to 85/87, ordered exact cases from 60/64 to 63/64, false-action cases from 3 to 0, and no-action specificity from 48/51 to 51/51. Required-call recall must remain 16/17. The known compiler-only おくれ miss and two harmless shared-fallback label errors are outside this variable and are expected to remain.
evidence_boundary: This is zero-model development on the consumed V58 holdout and its frozen model outputs. A pass can authorize only construction of a new independent V59 event-role holdout. It cannot establish fresh generalization, runtime readiness, physical safety, complete right-brain quality, or broad human likeness.

causal_isolation.tested_variable: Add only the V59 event-owner, directive-governor, and event-time relation graph over V58 state resolution before the same V57 compiler.
held_constant: consumed V58 holdout, item order, and all gold labels
grounded target ontology and mention patterns
one frozen fresh V51 fallback per target from the V58 raw report
V58 relations, commitment selector, and evidence anchors
V57 compiler, action allowlist, and ordered-call scorer

embedded_speech_content.condition: The grounded focus event appears inside question or complement content, while a later request marker governs a speech predicate such as teach, explain, tell, or answer rather than the focus event.

third_party_habitual_description.condition: An explicit third-party subject owns the focus event and habitual evidence marks a recurring plain description, with no request directly governing the focus event.

past_experiential_description.condition: Past or retrospective evidence places the focus event in a narrated experience owned by a third party or inferred non-addressee, with no request directly governing the focus event.

candidate_contract.direct_focus_request_protection: A request marker that directly governs the focus predicate must remain executable even when the sentence contains a past word, habitual adverb, or third-party object elsewhere.
candidate_contract.precedence: Existing V58 safety relations remain protected. V59 nonexecution relations may override only an otherwise requested local_directive-style result when direct_focus_request is false.

failure_routing.partial_fix: Reject V59 if any of the three prespecified false-action cases remains. Diagnose the missing owner, governor, or time relation without sentence-specific patches.
failure_routing.direct_request_regression: Reject V59 immediately if any V58-correct request or controlled contrast case is suppressed.
failure_routing.state_or_case_regression: Reject V59 if any previously correct target or exact case regresses, even when aggregate accuracy rises.
failure_routing.pass: Authorize construction of a new independent V59 event-role holdout only. Keep compiler coverage and model-size experiments separate.
